name: Artillery Firing Position

placement_rationale.text: 10 km places this inside real standing forest cover Pass 17 built on this side of the strip — a firing position doesn't just need to be within range, it needs overhead concealment from persistent drone ISR, which is exactly what a forest patch provides and open steppe doesn't. This is a first-class asset for the *position itself* (the dug-in pit, camouflage, ammunition dispersed nearby), distinct from the self-propelled gun assets already on this map, which represent the vehicles that occupy positions like this one and then displace after firing.

representative_system: Dug-in tube-artillery firing position under tree cover — composite, not a specific site

cost.display: Not a procurement item — a prepared position, not equipment

key_facts.label: Concealment
key_facts.value: Sited under canopy specifically to defeat persistent overhead drone ISR

key_facts.label: Doctrine
key_facts.value: "Shoot and scoot" — occupied briefly, not a fixed emplacement

key_facts.label: Threat
key_facts.value: Counter-battery radar and loitering munitions once the position fires and is located

short_role: The prepared, camouflaged ground a self-propelled or towed gun actually occupies to fire from — distinct from the gun itself.
characteristics: Sited inside real forest cover (this map's own Pass 17 terrain feature, not an assumed location) rather than open ground
Ammunition and camouflage netting dispersed around the position rather than stacked at one point
Occupied for a short window per fire mission under modern counter-battery/drone-ISR pressure, then vacated
Represents the position, not the piece — the self-propelled/towed gun assets on this map occupy positions like this one
employment_notes: Represents a generic firing position rather than a specific coordinate — the point is that real cover (forest, not open steppe) is what makes a position survivable long enough to fire a mission, not distance from the line alone. Guns rotate through positions like this one rather than occupying one permanently.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional artillery could mass in relatively open, fixed gun lines protected mainly by distance and counter-battery radar's own limits. Persistent drone ISR means an exposed position in open ground is found and struck within minutes of firing, which is why real cover — forest patches, not just standoff distance — has become load-bearing for artillery survivability.

connections.description: A position this gun occupies to fire a mission before displacing.
